subject: Visibility export and SIEM ingestion options for Redwood Private in ACME VPC
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <security-lead@acme-corp.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIEM ingestion + key mgmt questions for Private deployment

Hi Aditya / Laura,

Thanks for the quick onboarding yesterday — ACME is evaluating a pilot of Redwood Private inside our AWS VPC. Before we kick off the pilot we need to validate how telemetry (logs, metrics, traces) leaves our environment and what controls Redwood supports. A few concrete questions to start: 

- Can Redwood push logs/metrics/traces directly to our Splunk Cloud HEC endpoint over mTLS, or do you require a forwarder inside our network?
- Do you support restricting egress to a set of fixed IPs, or do we need to allow a range?
- How does token / key rotation work for HEC tokens and KMS-wrapped keys?
- Will any request/response content (prompts, caller data) be included in telemetry exports, or are those filtered?

Attached is a short questionnaire (acme-siem-questions.pdf) with required artifacts if possible (network diagram, recommended firewall rules, sample HEC config).

We'd like to scope a one-week pilot (dev->prod-mirroring) in our us-west-2 region. Can you outline a minimal firewall/egress config and a pilot checklist?

Thanks,
Jordan Ellis
Head of Security, Acme, Inc.
security-lead@acme-corp.com

---
From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <security-lead@acme-corp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIEM ingestion + key mgmt questions for Private deployment

Jordan — great questions. High level: we support three patterns for telemetry egress from Redwood Private; which one you choose depends on your compliance posture and network constraints. Summary below and I attached a draft playbook (visibility-export-playbook-v1.md) with config snippets.

Options (short):
1) Direct push to customer HEC (preferred when customer allows outbound TLS):
   - Redwood runtime opens outbound TLS (443) to your HEC FQDN.
   - Mutual TLS (mTLS) option available for HEC — we will present a cert bundle you install on your HEC endpoint for verification.
   - We rotate HEC tokens on a configurable schedule; token storage is in your KMS via key wrapping (we never persist raw tokens outside the private instance).

2) Customer-managed forwarder inside VPC (pull/push hybrid):
   - Deploy Vector / Fluentd as a sidecar or managed EC2 in your VPC that pulls from local ring buffer and forwards to Splunk.
   - No outbound connections required from Redwood to external endpoints; only to internal VPC forwarder.

3) S3 staging (for very restrictive networks):
   - Encrypted batches written to customer-owned S3 (VPC endpoint). Your downstream SIEM pulls from S3. Includes manifest and checkpointing.

Telemetry specifics:
- Logs/metrics: we export structured telemetry only (no raw prompt bodies). PII detection pipeline filters sensitive fields by default; any field-level redaction can be configured per-customer.
- Traces: OTEL/OTLP export supported. We recommend an OTEL collector in your VPC (either run by Redwood sidecar or by your infra) that accepts gRPC/HTTP and forwards to your tracing backend.
- Sampling: default adaptive sampler (0.5% tail on high volume workloads); pilot will set sampling to 5% full-trace capture for validation.

Networking & firewall (minimal):
- Allow outbound 443 to <your-hec-fqdn> (or to Redwood forwarder IPs if you prefer allowlisting).
- If using mTLS, add the Redwood CA cert to your HEC validation chain.

I attached sample HEC config and an OTEL snippet. Next step: propose a pilot checklist and a short call with your infra/security to validate firewall rules and key rotation.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

Attachments: visibility-export-playbook-v1.md, splunk-hec-sample-config.yaml, otel-collector-snippet.txt

Adding a few compliance and ops notes: 

- KMS & key wrapping: for Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) in their AWS account via cross-account KMS grants. This means HEC tokens are encrypted with a CMK you control and Redwood never has the plaintext key in our control plane. We'll provide the IAM role and grant document.
- Audit logs: accesses for config changes and token rotations are logged to the local audit log; we can stream those to your Splunk if you want an independent trail. Retention defaults to 90 days but can be bumped for SOC/PII requirements.
- Buffering: the runtime maintains a disk-backed ring buffer (configurable, default 5GB) to cover short egress outages. For long outages we checkpoint to S3 (customer-owned) before forwarding.

Marissa — can you prepare a short pilot checklist (network rules, sample Terraform for the forwarder, expected logs/metrics list) and a migration play for later? Vivek — please note potential infra tweaks: we may need to build a small configuration generator that emits the HEC TLS bundle and sample OTEL manifest for ACME region.

Laura Bennett
Head of Field Security, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups: 

- Firewall: we prefer allowlisting fixed IPs rather than FQDNs. Can you provide a stable list of Redwood egress IPs for us to add to the ACL? If not possible, we can host a small forwarder in our VPC.
- mTLS: we will do mTLS. Do you require client cert rotation on day 30/90? What is the recommended cadence?
- Pilot timing: thinking of starting pilot next Monday 2028-03-27. Can you confirm a time window for a 60–90m kickoff and which artifacts you'll deliver beforehand?

Ref: HubSpot case https://app.hubspot.com/cases/ACME-4412 (see requirement doc in attachments).

Jordan

Subject: Re: SIEM ingestion + key mgmt questions for Private deployment

Jordan — short plan and answers inline: 

- Egress IPs: for hosted Redwood we publish an allowlist, but for Private in-customer VPC the safest path is to run a tiny forwarder in your VPC and avoid Redwood egress entirely. That said we can also provide a small set of NAT egress IPs (TBD by infra) if you need Redwood-initiated TLS. I'll confirm by EOD Friday.
- mTLS cert rotation: recommended cadence is 90 days for client certs; tokens we rotate 30 days by default (configurable). We can support automated rotation via your KMS and an operator job in the cluster.
- Pilot deliverables (before kickoff):
   1) visibility-export-playbook-v1.md (detailed runbook + sample configs) — attached.
   2) splunk-hec-sample-config.yaml (HEC + mTLS snippet).
   3) otel-collector-snippet.txt (OTEL collector that exports OTLP -> HEC/tracing backend).
   4) pilot-checklist.xlsx (network rules, test plan, success criteria).

Pilot kickoff proposed: Mon 2028-03-27 10:00 PT — 90 minutes. Agenda: network validation (15m), deploy forwarder or HEC handshake (30m), smoke tests + telemetry validation (30m), wrap + next steps (15m).

Next steps: please confirm who from your infra/security will be on the call and if you prefer Redwood-initiated push or a VPC forwarder model. Once confirmed we'll upload the TLS cert bundle and sample Terraform for the forwarder into the HubSpot case.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
